Verdict

No confirmed indicators of a malicious supply-chain compromise were found. Overall risk: **info**.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • No evidence was found in the provided extraction for install-time execution via .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, or setup.py.
  • entry_points.txt only defines the memographix and mgx console scripts, which require explicit user invocation and are normal CLI entry points.
  • memographix/__init__.py only imports public models/workspace classes and defines __version__; no malicious import-time side effect is evident.
  • memographix/__main__.py invokes the CLI only when run as python -m memographix.
  • _native.pyd is imported conditionally by LocalEngine._scan_native() during indexing, not at package installation or interpreter startup based on the provided code.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • security.py contains regexes for .env, SSH keys, certificates, tokens, and password-like filenames, but the code uses them as filters to **skip sensitive files** during scanning. There is no evidence of broad credential harvesting, archive staging, or external exfiltration.
  • engine.py indexes repository files and stores local state under .memographix/graph.sqlite and .memographix/blobs/. This is consistent with the described local developer-tool behavior; no upload, webhook, or C2 endpoint evidence was found.
  • subprocess.run(["git", "diff", "--name-only", "HEAD"], ...) appears to be used to identify recently changed files. It does not by itself indicate token theft, command injection, or malicious automatic execution.
  • No evidence was found for persistence mechanisms such as systemd units, cron jobs, launch agents, shell profile edits, or startup folder registration.
  • No evidence was found for Kubernetes/CI/cloud lateral movement, Docker socket access, GitHub Actions token theft, or package registry token reuse.
  • Uses of ast.literal_eval and regexes appear related to configuration parsing and code-symbol extraction, not obfuscated loader or staged payload execution.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • The wheel contains memographix/_native.pyd, a native binary. However, this is consistent with WHEEL metadata showing Generator: maturin, Root-Is-Purelib: false, Tag: cp310-abi3-win_amd64, and METADATA indicating Rust support, so it is expected for a Rust/PyO3 Windows wheel.
  • The provided RECORD lists the native extension, Python files, SBOM, and license normally.
  • Within the provided materials, there is no clear evidence of typosquatting, hidden payloads, sudden malicious dependency insertion, or unexpected executable placement.

Additional Verification Needed

  • _native.pyd is binary and cannot be fully assessed from the provided text. Native static analysis, symbol/string review, and comparison against the Rust source/build output would be needed for higher confidence.
  • The sdist or GitHub source was not available here, so wheel/source behavior mismatch cannot be ruled out from this input alone.
  • The pre-scan reported a raw.items domain in config.py, but the provided config.py text does not corroborate any such network usage.
